```{r}
library(factoextra)
library(cluster)
library(fpc) 
library(FactoMineR) 
library(tidytext) 
```

```{r}
source("scripts/homemade_functions/homemade_clusterboot_function.R") # if apply_PCA is T, the hclust with be done on the PCs instead of the scores
source("scripts/homemade_functions/plot_top_loading.R") # for a PCA obj, plots the variables contributing most to the PC specified
source("scripts/homemade_functions/compute_vtest.R")
source("scripts/homemade_functions/plot_vtest_results.R")
source("scripts/homemade_functions/evaluate_nPC.R")
```


- **Purpose:** Create clusters based on the task scores
The median is used as score
Clustering is done both without and after PCA
- **Input:** wide score df
- **Output:** 
  - cluster asignments
  - plots
  
```{r}
load("data/processed/scores_wide.RData")

df_results_scores_wide <- df_results_scores_wide %>%
  column_to_rownames('sample')
```

```{r}
tasklist <- read.xlsx('data/SWAP_input/tasklist_test_gtex.xlsx')

tasklist_names <- tasklist %>%
  filter(!is.na(ID)) %>%
  dplyr::select(c('ID', 'DESCRIPTION', 'SHOULD.FAIL')) %>%
  mutate(ID = paste('task', ID, sep = '_'))
```

# Normalisation and scaling

```{r}
df_scores_scaled <- scale(log2(df_results_scores_wide), scale = T, center = T)
```

# Hierchichal clustering without PCA
```{r}
results_hclust <- hclust(dist(df_scores_scaled, method = 'euclidean'), method = 'ward.D2')

# tree
plot(, hang = -1)

# silouette
fviz_silhouette(silhouette(cutree(results_hclust, k=2), dist(df_scores_scaled, method = 'euclidean')))

# stability
clusterboot(df_scores_scaled,
            bootmethod = 'boot',
            distances= F,
            clustermethod = homemade_clusterboot_function,
            k=2, 
            B=500, seed=456)
```
From the tree there seems to be 2 clusters
Silouette for k=2 looks good with 0.25 and 0.42 average width
Stability is also decent with Jaccard 0.78 and 0.86

Run and plot vtest to see wich variables are different between clusters
```{r}
results_vtest <- compute_vtest(df=df_scores_scaled, 
                                 k=2, 
                                 hclust_obj = results_hclust)

plot_vtest_results(results_vtest %>% 
                   filter(adj_pval_BH <= 0.05))
```

# Hierchical clustering after PCA

```{r}
PCA <- prcomp(df_scores_scaled, center = F, scale = F) # data is already scaled and centered
```

```{r}
summary(PCA)
PCA$sdev^2 # eigenvalues
```
Some use the kaiser criteria (eigenvalue > 1) to choose how many PCs to keep for further analysis 
In this example only PC1 would meet this criteria, since we are working with only a few tasks

what variables are most important for the first 2 PCs
```{r}
plot_top_loading(PCA$rotation, dim_to_plot = 1, n_task = 3)
plot_top_loading(PCA$rotation, dim_to_plot = 2, n_task = 3)
```

## clustering on the first 2 PCs
```{r}
results_hclust_2PC <- hclust(dist(PCA$x[, 1:2], method = 'euclidean'), method = 'ward.D2')

# tree
plot(results_hclust_2PC, hang = -1)
rect.hclust(results_hclust_2PC, k = 2, border = 2:4)

table(cutree(results_hclust_2PC, k = 2))  

# silouette
fviz_silhouette(silhouette(cutree(results_hclust_2PC, k=2), dist(PCA$x[, 1:2], method = 'euclidean')))

# stability
clusterboot(df_scores_scaled,
            bootmethod = 'boot',
            distances= F,
            clustermethod = homemade_clusterboot_function,
            k=2, apply_PCA = T, nPC=2, 
            B=500, seed=456)
```
From the tree would be 2 clusters again
Silouette is 0.37 and 0.55
Stability (Jaccard) is 0.79 and 0.86
Overall a bit better than without PCA

Run and plot vtest to see wich variables are different between clusters
```{r}
results_vtest_2PC <- compute_vtest(df=df_scores_scaled, 
                                 k=2, 
                                 hclust_obj = results_hclust_2PC)

plot_vtest_results(results_vtest_2PC %>% 
                   filter(adj_pval_BH <= 0.05))
```

## Evaluating the number of PCs to keep after PCA
In this example with only a few tasks it is less relevant,
but for >100 tasks looking at how the results vary when changing the number of PCs kept is informative
```{r}
results_various_n_PCs_PCA <- lapply(c(2,4,5,6), evaluate_nPC, df_scores = df_scores_scaled, k_max = 3) %>%
  do.call('rbind', .)

results_various_n_PCs_PCA %>%
  filter(k==2)

results_various_n_PCs_PCA %>%
  filter(k==3)
```
